newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAB eyes Uganda brewery, Ghana talks fail.
newsitem.headline: SAB eyes Uganda brewery, Ghana talks fail.

text.p: South African Breweries Ltd (SAB) said on Monday that it was in talks to buy a stake in a Ugandan brewery as a further part of its African expansion.
SAB is holding discussions with Madhvani Group for a stake in Nile Breweries, which has a 60 percent share of Uganda's annual beer market of 700,000 hectolitres.
"It is certainly at the talks stage...all things going really well, I would say perhaps by September (a deal will be struck)," Andre Parker, managing director of SAB's beer interests, told Reuters.
Parker said negotiations were at a sensitive stage and he could not reveal any financial details of the possible purchase.

SAB already has stakes in the beer markets of Uganda's East African neighbours Tanzania, where it owns 46 percent of Tanzania Breweries, and Kenya, where it is building a $45 million brewery near Nairobi.
Uganda has caught foreign investors' eyes recently with its healthy economic growth and Parker said it was important for SAB to move into the market.
"Uganda, in terms of its economic potential, is probably the brightest of the states in that region," he said.

SAB, which dominates the South African market, has won market praise for its ambitious expansion in Eastern and Central Europe with moves in Poland, Hungary and Romania. It also has joint ventures in China.
But more recently the firm has turned its eyes back to its home continent.
SAB is also currently in talks in Angola and Ethiopia and has handed a proposal to the Namibian government to build a 100 million rand production plant in the northern town of Oshakati.
With a planned capacity of 250,000 hectolitres of beer a year, the brewery could supply up to 40 percent of the former German colony's estimated market, until now dominated by Namibian Breweries.
However, the firm has suffered a setback in its plans to move for the first time into West Africa as negotiations on a possible deal in Ghana have come to an end.
Parker said he was unable to comment further on what had been planned in Ghana but the firm would still be keen to invest there should a suitable opportunity arise.
"We have not forgotten about West Africa," he said.
Ghana was seen as important to the firm as it would provide a base for a possible future launch into the potentially lucrative markets of Francophone Africa.
Industry sources said SAB had made a bid for Ghana's ABC Brewery but had been pipped at the post by Dutch brewer Heineken NV.
